speaker: lead
text: Okay, let's get started. Today's meeting is about getting ready for the office move. You've all heard we're moving to a new office, right?

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, I heard we're going to a new building in Pangyo. I stopped by briefly last week, and the ceilings are high, so it feels a lot more spacious.

speaker: member_c
text: I saw the photos too. The windows are big. I heard there's a convenience store and a café on the first floor.

speaker: member_b
text: There's apparently a gym in the basement too, and it's free for tenant employees.

speaker: lead
text: A gym, even? Then everyone will actually get some exercise.

speaker: member_a
text: Some people's commutes will get a bit longer, though. Mine goes up by about twenty minutes on the subway.

speaker: member_c
text: Mine actually gets shorter. It's just one bus.

speaker: lead
text: Nice. Well, there's a lot to prepare, so let's go through it one by one. First, let's decide when we move.

speaker: member_a
text: The building said we can move in from December. If we move on a weekday, work stops, so a weekend would be better.

speaker: member_b
text: The first Saturday in December is the 6th, and the second Saturday is the 13th.

speaker: member_c
text: The second week is when year-end event prep starts, so it might be pretty hectic. I'd prefer the first week.

speaker: member_a
text: The first week for me too. I'd feel better moving early and getting settled.

speaker: lead
text: Then let's go with Saturday, December 6th. Everyone okay with that?

speaker: member_b
text: Yes, sounds good.

speaker: member_c
text: Yes.

speaker: lead
text: Next is how we arrange the seating. We'll have a whole floor in the new office, so this is a chance to change things up.

speaker: member_b
text: I'd like to keep sitting together by team like we do now. Work goes faster when the person you need to ask is right next to you.

speaker: member_c
text: I think hot-desking could work too. We work from home a lot these days, so desks are often empty anyway.

speaker: member_b
text: With hot-desking, I feel like we'd waste time every morning looking for a desk. And we'd have to carry our stuff around every time.

speaker: member_a
text: If we get lockers, that solves the stuff problem. A lot of other companies do it that way.

speaker: member_c
text: There's also the question of who gets the window seats. With fixed seats, the people who've been here longest always end up taking them.

speaker: member_b
text: That seems like a different issue. Even with fixed seats, we could just draw lots.

speaker: member_a
text: How many meeting rooms are there? Right now there aren't enough, so booking one is always a battle.

speaker: member_b
text: Apparently two large rooms and four small ones. That's about twice what we have now.

speaker: member_c
text: Then it'd be nice to have small rooms for phone calls. Taking calls at your desk bothers the people around you.

speaker: lead
text: Hmm, opinions are pretty split. We need to hear what each team leader thinks too, so I'll collect their views separately and we'll talk about it again.

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, that sounds good.

speaker: member_c
text: Oh, that reminds me, what time does the cafeteria in the new building open?

speaker: member_b
text: From eleven thirty, I heard. There are two menus, and on Fridays they serve a special.

speaker: member_c
text: A special sounds great. Our current building has no cafeteria, so going out to eat every day was a chore.

speaker: member_a
text: How much does the cafeteria cost, though?

speaker: member_b
text: Six thousand won a meal, apparently. That's half of what it costs to eat out.

speaker: lead
text: We'll save a bit on meals, then. What about parking? A few people drive in.

speaker: member_b
text: There's an underground parking lot, but it's limited to five cars per tenant. General Affairs said they'll take applications separately.

speaker: member_a
text: Oh, but about the December 6th date we picked earlier. I just saw a notice from building management, and the new building has scheduled elevator maintenance that day.

speaker: lead
text: Elevator maintenance? Then we can't get our things upstairs.

speaker: member_a
text: Right, all elevators are shut down from nine a.m. to six p.m. We can't carry everything up the stairs.

speaker: lead
text: Then the 6th won't work. We'll have to look at the date again.

speaker: member_c
text: Is there maintenance on the 13th?

speaker: member_a
text: The notice only mentions the 6th. The 13th looks fine.

speaker: member_b
text: Earlier you said the second week was tough because of year-end event prep, but if it's a Saturday, wouldn't that be okay?

speaker: member_c
text: If it's a Saturday, it's fine for me too. We can do the event prep on weekdays.

speaker: lead
text: Then let's push it back a week and go with Saturday, December 13th.

speaker: member_a
text: Okay, the 13th it is.

speaker: member_b
text: Sounds good.

speaker: lead
text: Next is the moving company. Kenji, you got some quotes, right?

speaker: member_b
text: Yes, I got quotes from three places. Company A is the cheapest, Company B is in the middle, and Company C is the most expensive.

speaker: member_c
text: How big is the price difference?

speaker: member_b
text: There's about a million won between Company A and Company C. But looking at reviews for Company A, there were some complaints about things getting damaged.

speaker: member_a
text: We have a lot of monitors and server equipment, so damage would be a real problem.

speaker: member_b
text: Company B does special packing for IT equipment. And they're only about three hundred thousand won more than Company A.

speaker: member_c
text: How are Company B's reviews?

speaker: member_b
text: Their reviews were the best. The team next door used Company B when they moved last year, and they said there were no problems.

speaker: lead
text: Since IT equipment came up, let's also look at how we move the network and the PCs.

speaker: member_a
text: I asked the IT team, and they said they'll move the network equipment and PCs themselves on Friday night, and get everything connected by Saturday morning.

speaker: member_c
text: So we can start working right away Monday morning?

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, and they said they'll do a check on Saturday afternoon too.

speaker: member_b
text: If it's Friday night, everyone will need to shut down their PCs before leaving that day.

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, the IT team said they'll send out a message asking everyone to save their work and shut down by five p.m. Friday.

speaker: member_b
text: Then the moving company only needs to move the desks, cabinets and personal stuff, not the IT equipment. That should bring the quote down a bit.

speaker: member_c
text: But the moving company will still move the monitors, right? The monitors are what I'm most worried about.

speaker: member_a
text: The IT team will move the monitors along with the PCs.

speaker: lead
text: Good. Then let's settle both: we'll go with Company B, and the IT team will move the network and PCs first on Friday night.

speaker: member_b
text: Okay, I'll contact Company B today and tell them we'll sign.

speaker: member_a
text: I'll let the IT team know Friday night is confirmed.

speaker: member_c
text: And when should we let our clients know the address is changing? Quite a few documents come by courier or mail.

speaker: member_b
text: A lot of original contracts still come by mail. If the address changes, they could get sent back.

speaker: member_a
text: Don't we also need to update the address on the website and our business cards?

speaker: member_b
text: We're keeping the main phone number, right? If the number changes too, it becomes a much bigger job.

speaker: member_a
text: We can keep the phone number, apparently. It's an internet phone line.

speaker: member_c
text: Business cards are cheaper to print all at once, so we can order them after the date is final.

speaker: lead
text: For letting clients know, I think we should first hear how the sales team wants to handle it. I'll talk to the head of sales.

speaker: member_b
text: Yes, sales handles some clients separately anyway.

speaker: member_c
text: Then let's look at that again next week.

speaker: member_a
text: Oh, right, what about the old document boxes in the storage room here? Are we taking all of those too?

speaker: lead
text: Let's shred everything past its retention period this time. I'll ask General Affairs to call in a shredding company.

speaker: member_b
text: Good. There must be more than fifty boxes.

speaker: member_c
text: There are a lot of plants too. Everyone can just take their own, right?

speaker: lead
text: Yes, let's have everyone take care of their own plants and personal things.

speaker: lead
text: Okay, we're almost out of time. Let me go over what we decided today.

speaker: lead
text: The move is Saturday, December 13th, the moving company is Company B, and the IT team moves the network and PCs first on Friday night.

speaker: lead
text: For seating and letting clients know, I'll talk to the team leaders and the sales team, and we'll look at it again next week.

speaker: member_a
text: Okay, I'll write up the minutes and post them.

speaker: lead
text: Thanks. Good work, everyone.
